subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should existing-agent workspace relocation become a public CLI setter, and should that be a new `agents set-workspace`/`agents update --workspace` command rather than changing `set-identity --workspace` semantics?
rationale: Both an output-only clarification and a dedicated setter are plausible, but the choice changes public CLI semantics and JSON compatibility while current docs define `--workspace` as a locator/selector.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add a documented existing-agent workspace update command backed by `agents.update`, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Output Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add or rename response fields so `set-identity` cannot be read as confirming a stored workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` update stored workspace too, accepting compatibility risk against the current help and docs.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add a documented existing-agent workspace update command backed by `agents.update`, and make `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The original identity CLI helper and public output shape trace to this owner path, and the remaining choice is the public CLI contract.
